claims.statement: Each persisted Claim evidence record pairs a canonical resource identity with an opaque resolver-owned version token observed when the Claim was established, and reconciliation compares these tokens for equality without interpreting them.

runClaimsPreflight loads every persisted page sidecar and resolves each Claim evidence resource against its recorded version once per preflight, classifying resources as unresolved when the resolver returns nothing or throws an EvidenceSecurityError and as changed when it returns a different version token.

A persisted Claim with any unresolved resource (including an EvidenceSecurityError) emits an 'unresolved' GroundingIssue while a Claim with only changed resources emits a 'stale' issue, and preflight sorts its issues deterministically by page, kind, and claim id.

Preflight lets non-security evidence resolution errors propagate so a transient failure is never mistaken for deleted evidence, but catches EvidenceSecurityError (raised when an evidence path traverses a symbolic link or filesystem alias outside the repository root) and records the cited resource as unresolved instead of aborting the run, so a symlinked-evidence Claim is routed to the page worker for reconciliation; preflight also inventories orphan sidecars whose generated pages no longer exist.

getUpdateNoopStatus refuses to skip an update when there is no previous update git head, when the previous run was interrupted, when the requested language's primary subtag differs from the persisted wiki language's primary subtag, when the working tree has meaningful changes, or when committed changes since the last update touch source outside openwiki/ and outside the openWikiIgnore boundary; it resolves the requested language via requireResolvedLanguage (a defensive boundary check that throws if an unrecognized value slipped past an entry point) before comparing primary subtags, and treats a primary-language-subtag change as meaningful rather than a skip.

The repository run performs Claims validation before update no-op detection and, when force is not requested, skips only when getUpdateNoopStatus reports shouldSkip, the Claims runtime reports issueCount === 0, and every initial page already has baseline manifest coverage (hasCompleteBaselineCoverage); a force update bypasses the whole no-op gate, and stale or unresolved Claims or incomplete baseline coverage force an update to proceed even on an otherwise clean tree.

When the Git preflight, a zero Claims issue count, and complete baseline coverage all allow a skip, the run snapshots the source, finalizes Claims, re-snapshots to prove the fingerprint is stable, replaces the page manifest with the stable checkpoint, re-snapshots the published source, and only then rewrites last-update metadata before returning a noop result; any drift between snapshots falls out of the no-op and the run proceeds to planning.

During plan normalization addRequiredClaimIssueJobs groups outstanding grounding issues by page and inserts a pending page job for any affected page not already planned or deleted, deriving that job's seed paths from the issue resources by stripping the repo:// scheme and #Lx-Ly line fragment.

The required-page job inserted for stale or unresolved Claims instructs the worker to reconcile those Claims and update the page from current repository evidence while preserving unaffected accurate content, so a staleness marker triggers a source recheck rather than an automatic retraction.

When a page worker submits its finished page, submitRepositoryPage repairs and validates front matter (rejecting unrepairable front matter as invalid_input), then under the run-mutation lock calls reconcilePageClaims with the worker's sparse Claim decisions, persists the page's dirty Claim state via finalize with the run's startedAt timestamp (excluding otherPendingPages — every other job still pending plus deferredClaimPages — so a concurrent worker's transient bytes or a deferred page's unsettled issues are not projected into verification stamps or rehashed sidecars), and asserts the page's Claims are durable via assertPageClaimsDurable before recording the completion and advancing the queue; any failure in that block that is not already a RepositoryRunError is wrapped in a RepositoryRunError with invalid_input.

reconcilePageClaims normalizes each proposed Claim by trimming its statement and trimming, deduplicating, and sorting its evidence resources so evidence is compared as an order-independent set, and it rejects a payload whose claims entries contain two identical statement-plus-evidence fingerprints.

A proposal that reuses an existing Claim id with unchanged statement and evidence, or an id-less proposal whose content exactly matches an existing Claim, is reconciled to a confirm operation that preserves the stable id.
A confirm or an update that retains evidence re-resolves the Claim's current evidence resources, which refreshes the persisted version tokens to current source.
A proposal that reuses an existing id but changed its statement, evidence, or both is reconciled to an update carrying only the changed fields, preserving the Claim id.
A proposal with no id and no exact match to an existing Claim is reconciled to an add operation for which OpenWiki allocates a fresh globally unique identifier.

reconcilePageClaims rejects a proposal that names a Claim id not owned by the page or that reuses the same existing id twice across any sparse field (confirmedClaimIds, claims, retractedClaimIds) via the targetExisting helper.

applyClaimOperations is an all-or-nothing mutation boundary that validates operations first, rejects unknown ids and any id targeted more than once per batch, pre-resolves all evidence before touching a cloned working set, and returns updated claims only on success so a mid-batch resolution failure leaves session state unchanged.

Focused tests pin the sparse reconciliation contract: one call omits an issue-free Claim, revises another by id, adds a third without an id, and retracts an omitted one with stable ids preserved; an empty payload preserves every current statement; a worker cannot paraphrase an omitted unchanged Claim while adding another; a stale Claim omitted from the payload is rejected until it receives an explicit decision; duplicate sparse proposals, conflicting decisions on the same id, and a page left with zero final Claims are rejected; an already-absent retraction is an idempotent retry; fingerprint delimiters do not conflate distinct Claims; a proposal or retraction naming another page's id is rejected; and a mid-batch evidence resolution failure leaves session state unchanged.

finalize accepts an excludedPages set (empty by default) and skips every page it names, persists only dirty non-excluded pages, refuses to persist a page carrying unresolved evidence debt, and rechecks each dirty page's evidence against current source and re-hashes its Markdown before writing the sidecar.

finishRepositoryRun validates that every skipped page job has exactly one matching original page snapshot (by job id and path) before any work, throwing invalid_state otherwise, then derives skippedPages from those jobs plus the plan's deferredClaimPages; it restores skipped-page Markdown from snapshots first and only afterward calls finalize and assertRepositoryClaimsDurable with skippedPages as excludedPages, so skipped and deferred pages are excluded from final Claims persistence and the whole-run durability proof, records the run as interrupted rather than complete when any pages were skipped or deferred or source drifted, and restamps the page manifest with the current run's source checkpoint only for pages the run actually regenerated (entries whose completedRunId equals run.state.runId), while skipped, deferred, and untouched pages retain their prior checkpoint and provenance through replaceRepositoryPageManifest's preserveSourcePages branch (a page whose bytes changed under deterministic finalization still refreshes its pageVersion).

The Claims runtime finalize delegates to ClaimSession.finalize with the producer actor and timestamp, then appends a finalizeVerificationProjection step (which synchronizes verification metadata, refreshes page versions for every represented page, and rolls back unsafe stamps) and throws a ClaimsPersistenceError if any finalization warnings remain.

reconcilePageClaims auto-confirms every existing issue-free Claim omitted from the sparse payload, and throws invalid_input for any stale or unresolved Claim that did not receive an explicit confirm, update, or retract decision, so issue markers force a source recheck rather than silent retention or automatic retraction.

reconcilePageClaims rejects a completed factual page whose reconciled result would retain or establish zero Claims (existing count minus retracted plus added equals zero), enforcing that every factual page owns at least one material Claim.

A retractedClaimId that the page no longer owns and that no page in the session owns is silently skipped, so retraction is idempotent across retries after the first submission reached durable Claims persistence but later page-job checkpointing failed.

nextRepositoryPage enriches the first pending job with mode, whether the page exists, existingClaimCount, and claimsRequiringAttention (the page's issue-bearing Claims projected without opaque evidence versions), so the worker is told which Claims require an explicit decision without repeating issue-free ones.

inspectRepositoryPageClaims returns the complete compact Claim set (without opaque evidence versions) for the current pending page only and throws invalid_state for any other job; it backs the inspect_claims tool that workers call on demand before intentionally revising or removing otherwise-current content, and ordinary focused updates should not call it.

CLAIMS_RECONCILIATION_GUIDANCE is the shared model-facing sparse-reconciliation standard embedded in both the native agent page-worker prompt and the MCP host instructions, codifying that stale or unresolved markers require an explicit decision, omitted issue-free Claims are retained, and the final page body and reconciled Claim set must agree.

assertPageClaimsDurable proves a page's Claims, page version, and verification are durable by loading the persisted sidecar, re-hashing the current Markdown against pageVersion, requiring a verification record and confirming it was projected into the page's verified frontmatter field, then running a session-projection comparison in which inspectClaims(page) is authoritative: a persisted-count mismatch fails, and every session Claim must match a persisted claim by id, identical statement, and an order-independent sameResourceSet evidence comparison (resources deduplicated and sorted by UTF-16 code-unit order, comparing resource identity not version tokens); assertRepositoryClaimsDurable extends this to the whole run by rejecting orphan sidecars whose Markdown no longer exists and iterating the session's getEvidenceResourcesByPage projection (skipping excludedPages and pages whose session Claim count is zero) to call assertPageClaimsDurable for every remaining claimed page.

The resolver owns and interprets line-range evidence versions distinctly from the opaque comparison used by preflight and the durability proofs. A whole-file resource versions as a SHA-256 of the complete file content (repo-file-v1), so any edit changes the token; a line-range resource (repo://path#Lx-Ly) versions as a content hash plus resolver-owned relocation metadata (repo-lines-v1) recording the selected line count, first/last selected-line hashes, and up to three lines of preceding/following context. locateUnchangedLineRange re-finds a moved-but-unchanged block by content hash and context anchors and returns the same version (so the Claim stays current and produces no stale issue); locateChangedLineRange relocates a changed block between its unchanged exterior anchors and returns a new version (stale); when anchors are ambiguous or the block cannot be safely relocated the resolver returns null (unresolved).

No-op detection is only consulted when the run carries no explicit user request: shouldCheckUpdateNoop is true only when userMessage is empty, and the native driver derives force from Boolean(userMessage.trim()) while passing the message as planningContext, so a user-driven update always bypasses the no-op gate. When planningContext is non-empty the planner prompt adds a hard scoped-update mandate: the planner schedules only directly requested pages/files and genuinely affected cross-references or navigation, preserves unrelated page framing and the information architecture, and does not refresh /openwiki/quickstart.md unless the user explicitly requests it or the page map, navigation, or task-routing links actually change.

The submit_page tool surfaces invalid_input rejections as retryable rather than fatal: when submitRepositoryPage throws a RepositoryRunError with code invalid_input, the runner converts it into an error-status ToolMessage (via createSubmissionRejection) carrying the error code, message, and a concrete next-step instruction, keeping the worker loop active so the model can repair and resubmit. Any other error (a not_found/invalid_state failure, or a non-RepositoryRunError thrown by the store itself) sets a fatal flag and is re-thrown so the worker is not retried and the run stops. A submit_page that already succeeded throws if the model calls it again.

A focused update may submit deferUnplannedClaimIssues: true in ProposedRepositoryPlan to skip required Claim-issue job injection; createRepositoryPlan then omits addRequiredClaimIssueJobs and instead derives deferredClaimPages — the issue-bearing pages the planner neither generated nor deleted — which are folded into skippedPages at finishRepositoryRun and into otherPendingPages at submitRepositoryPage, so their stale/unresolved Claim issues are left for a later full update and the pages are excluded from finalization and the whole-run durability proof. Init runs reject deferUnplannedClaimIssues with invalid_input, and required rewrite jobs are still injected regardless of the flag.
